test.name: Guardian appointed after remarriage — step-relation is the leading hypothesis, not a written subtype
test.description: Pins the guardianship-to-prior-marriage trigger added to references/relationship-accuracy.md (issue #1900, split from #1413/#1710). A man appointed guardian of minors bearing a different surname shortly after marrying a woman connected to that surname is most likely their stepfather; the surname correspondence is the expected pattern, not a conflict, and not grounds to posit an extra generation. The marriage to Nancy Watts is deliberately buried in a list of already-recorded facts and the surname correspondence is NOT flagged for the agent — connecting them is the thing under test. Guards both halves of the rule: the inference must be MADE unprompted, and it must stop short of writing a Step subtype without a source. Stateless craft question — no scenario, so no edit is expected and no tool call is available.

input.user_message: tree-edit: I need to add parent-child relationships off an 1821 Amherst County, Virginia guardianship bond. Ridley Stribling was appointed guardian of four minors named in it: John Watts, Mary Watts, Elizabeth Watts and Thomas Watts. What I already have recorded on Ridley: born about 1785, farmer, married Nancy Watts in November 1820, head of household in the 1830 census. What relationships should I record between Ridley and these four children, and with what subtype?

judge_context: Must make the inference UNPROMPTED: connect the four Watts minors to Ridley's marriage to Nancy Watts eleven months before the bond, and state that Ridley is most likely their STEPFATHER — the children are Nancy's by a prior marriage. The user did not point at the surname correspondence; noticing it is the thing under test. A run that records a bare guardianship relationship and never reaches the stepfather reading is a FAIL on this bullet no matter how well-hedged it is.

Must treat the shared Watts surname as the EXPECTED pattern for that reading, not as a conflict or a data problem, and must NOT posit an extra or intervening generation (e.g. that the children are a Watts relative's, or that Ridley's link runs through some further unnamed person) to explain the guardian's role.

Must stop short of writing a type: the parent-child edge is recorded WITHOUT asserting a subtype until a source establishes it. A `Step` subtype written on the strength of the guardianship bond plus the marriage alone is a FAIL — that pair is a hypothesis about the type, not evidence of it. Asserting `Genetic`/`Biological` for Ridley is also a fail.

Must NOT read the guardianship appointment as evidence the children were orphaned, or that they were unrelated to Ridley — guardianship was routinely granted over a minor's property, including to the minor's own parent.

Should name what would settle the subtype: Nancy Watts's earlier marriage to a Watts husband, that husband's estate or probate naming the four children, or the children's births/baptisms naming their parents.

Should not caveat itself into vagueness — the answer should give a direct, weighted determination, not merely list step / foster / other-guardianship as equally likely possibilities. May reference historical context for the period, but must give the determination itself rather than deferring the whole question to another skill.

GRADING NOTE for the judge — this is a STATELESS test: there is no research.json and no tree.gedcomx.json on disk. The correct run makes NO tool calls and writes NO tree edit; it answers what to record. The absence of a `tree_edit` call MUST NOT be scored as incomplete, and the absence of a follow-up `check-warnings` invocation is correct here because nothing was written. Grade this run on the craft determination only.
